text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Aston Villa and Arsenal at Villa Park!
It's been a stellar season for Villa so far, and they're looking to close the gap to the top of the table with another win here.
They've lost just one of their last 13 games in all competitions (W10 D2), but it's their home form that is turning a lot of heads.

Their dominant 1-0 win over Manchester City on Wednesday saw them leapfrog Pep Guardiola's side into third and extend their winning run at home in the league to 14 games - they've never before in their history won 15 consecutive games on home soil.
Arsenal were the last side to come away from Villa Park with three points after their 4-2 win back in February.
They're in good form themselves and they're looking to go back to the top of the table with another victory here after Liverpool's win over Crystal Palace earlier today.
They've won their last six on the bounce in all competitions, extending that run in dramatic fashion as Declan Rice's stoppage-time goal snatched a 4-3 win over Luton Town on Tuesday.
Unsurprisingly, Unai Emery sticks with the same starting line-up that blew City away on Wednesday.
Bailey, who scored the winner in that game, has shaken off the issue that forced him off late on to retain his place.
There's just one change by Arsenal from their win over Luton last time out.
Zinchenko comes in at left-back for Kiwior, who drops to the bench.
They will also be without Mikel Arteta on the touchline after he picked up his third booking of the season during the celebrations on Tuesday.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Jesus gets the game under way for Arsenal!
Arsenal try to make a quick start to the game, but Havertz is dispossessed in the box.
Villa work it straight down the other end to win a corner, but Bailey's cross is cleared at the near post by Jesus.
Saliba and Watkins are challenging to bring a long pass down, and Raya comes up behind them to join in.
He looks a little shaky as the ball slips through his gloves, but luckily for him, Villa can't pounce on the loose ball.
CHANCE! After soaking up a good spell of Villa pressure, Arsenal break quickly, and Saka goes for the big switch out to Martinelli on the left.
He returns the favour, whipping a good cross to the far post, but Saka can't reach it properly on the stretch.
MCGINN SCORES! What a start for Villa! Bailey starts the move on the right, squeezing between three defenders before continuing his run, so he can get it back from Tielemans.
He weaves through players before squaring it to McGinn, who neatly turns to face goal before rifling his shot into the far top corner.
1-0 Villa!
It's a brilliant bit of play from Bailey, and Gabriel wasn't sure if he was trying to shoot or cross.
He leaves the defender in a bit of a tangle as he pulls it back to the Villa captain.
Arteta does not look happy up in the stands, but Arsenal are trying to get a quick response here.
Martinelli pushes his way down the left once more, but the cross is poor this time as Carlos clears his lines.
Just like against City on Wednesday, Villa aren't giving Arsenal a lot of time on the ball, and are closing down the space the visitors want to play through.
Martinelli has another run down the wing, but takes it out of play.
Arsenal are enjoying a good spell of possession here, but their final pass is just letting them down at the moment.
Zinchenko played his too close to Martinez, while Rice's attempted throughball is too heavy for Saka.
McGinn has scored four goals in the Premier League this season, his most in a single campaign in the competition.
He only netted once in 34 league games for Villa last season.
Kamara is caught on the ball in the centre circle by Havertz, who quickly breaks on the counter.
He unselfishly tees up Saka, who sees his shot blocked by Torres on the edge of the box.
Zinchenko is popping up all over the pitch, and this time he tries to thread it through the middle for Havertz to chase.
Konsa just gets his body in front of the ball, and wins a free-kick when the German drags him down.
Villa mount another good counter after soaking up a spell of Arsenal pressure, and Havertz tugs Tielemans' shirt.
Villa have a free-kick in a good position here.
The free-kick is about 30 yards out, and it's Digne who steps up.
He curls his cross straight into the wall, and Luiz blasts his follow-up into the exact same place.
Saka peels off the back of Digne in the box, and he draws Martinez out to the byline.
The winger manages to pull it back into the middle, but luckily for the hosts, it's Carlos who meets it.
There's a nervy moment at the back for Villa as it's knocked back to Martinez, who takes a heavy touch.
None of the Arsenal players were putting pressure on though, so the keeper had the chance to coolly get things moving once more.
Tielemans spins away from Zinchenko, and the left-back grabs a fistful of his shirt to drag him down.
He's shown the first booking of the game.
There's only been one shot on target in this game - McGinn's goal - and things are still fairly cagey here.
Both sides are struggling to break their opponents down at the moment, as White's run is flagged for offside in Arsenal's latest attack.
SAVE! Villa just play themselves into trouble here, with Watkins cheaply gifting the ball to Odegaard.
He slides it through to Saka, who takes the shot first time, but it's curled straight at Martinez.
JUST WIDE! White takes the corner short to Saka, who shapes to cross only to square it to Odegaard.
He knocks it past Torres before taking on the shot, but he drags it inches wide of the near post.
Arsenal are just starting to up the pressure now, with Villa struggling to get out of their own half.
They look to Martinelli down the left once more, but his cross is behind Jesus.
OFF THE LINE! Martinelli times his run perfectly on the left to get on the end of the long ball, and the keeper rushes off his line.
The Brazilian dinks it over him, but Carlos races across to clear it off the line.
Villa are dropping deeper and deeper into their own half as Arsenal ramp up the pressure once more.
Martinelli threatens to break down the left again, but Konsa clears his lines.
SAVE! Rice wins the ball back and sets Havertz away down the left.
He surges forward before squaring it to Saka, and his deft touch sets Odegaard up nicely.
He hits his low shot first time, but Martinez gets behind it.
SAVE! Jesus overruns the ball and touches it to Luiz in an attempt to make up for it.
He works it through Tielemans to pick out Watkins, but his shot is smothered by Raya.
The flag did go up against him, but the forward had timed his run.
GOOD SAVE! Zinchenko plays another good ball over the top, this time to pick out Jesus' run off the back of Carlos.
He cuts inside before whipping a shot on goal, but Martinez stretches to push it away.
Saka's first corner is flicked over the bar at the near post by Konsa, and Arsenal get another chance to whip it in.
The second is curled straight into Martinez's gloves, but Rice feels he could've had a penalty as he goes down under pressure from Torres.
Saliba is being put under pressure by Watkins and plays a blind backpass that gives away an unnecessary corner.
Bailey whips it into the near post but doesn't clear the first man again as White heads it away.
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 1-0 ARSENAL.
McGinn's early goal gives Villa a 1-0 lead over Arsenal at half-time.
The hosts couldn't have asked for a better start to the game as Bailey's trickery helped to set McGinn up to rifle in the opener just seven minutes in.
The game slowed a bit after that, but Arsenal started to find their rhythm after the half-hour mark.
Martinez made important saves to keep out Saka, Odegaard and Jesus, while Martinelli saw a shot cleared off the line after drawing the keeper off his line and dinking it over him.
Since taking the early lead, Villa haven't been able to cause Arsenal too many problems.

They have a great record when taking the lead though, as they haven't lost any of the last 20 Premier League games in which they've opened the scoring (W18 D2), winning each of the last nine in a row.
Arteta clearly wasn't happy with how his side started the game, and he'll be looking for them to pick up where they left off to get back into this game.
Villa are making a change at the break.
About halfway through the first half, Bailey wasn't moving too comfortably.
It looks like Emery isn't taking any chances as he replaces him with Diaby.
Villa get us back under way for the second half!
Jesus is down in the box asking for a penalty after being caught by Luiz.
Both players had their feet up to get the ball, and the midfielder caught him a little late.
There's not much in it, and after a quick VAR check, there's still no spot-kick.
There are shouts from the home fans for a penalty now for a handball against Gabriel.
McGinn's cross was poor, and the defender blocked it, but his arm was down by his side and the referee waves play on.

Arsenal have only come back to win one of their last 21 Premier League away games in which they've trailed at half-time (D4 L16), although that one victory came in this exact fixture last season, winning 4-2 at Villa Park (1-2 at the break).
Digne gets too tight to Saka and then tugs him back when the winger gets away.
He's booked, and it's a costly yellow card that will see him miss next weekend's game against Brentford.
Arsenal's high press is causing all sorts of problems here as Kamara is outmuscled by Martinelli on the edge of his own box.
The ball bounces kindly towards Jesus, but Martinez rushes out to prevent a shot.
Villa are making another change here.
Tielemans is taken off, with Ramsey on in his place.
OFF THE LINE! Saka whips another corner into the six-yard box and Martinez parries it instead of catching.
It bounces off Watkins back, and Carlos is on the line once more to preserve Villa's clean sheet.
MISS! Arsenal should be level! Zinchenko dinks it over the top once more, and Havertz gets in front of Ramsey to lift it into the middle.
Odegaard runs onto it, hitting the shot first time, but gets it all wrong as it bounces wide of the far post.
Villa just can't get out of their own half at the moment, and they're struggling to get on the ball too.
Arsenal are dominating possession, but struggling to get any results to show for it.
NO GOAL! Arsenal work it out from the back again, and Rice lifts it over the top for Saka to chase as he peels off the back of Digne.
Martinez comes racing out of his box, but Saka takes it around him before slotting into the empty net, but the flag is up against him.
Luiz just clips the back of Saka's heels but then throws the ball away in frustration.
It's a silly booking to pick up, especially since it's his fifth of the season, so he'll miss the Brentford game too.
The space just seems to open up for Diaby down the right, and he's allowed to carry the ball a long way.
He doesn't have support in the box, but he curls in a low cross anyway, which Raya holds onto.
Emery is making a double change this time as he tries to gain some control in the game.
Konsa is the first to go off, with Cash coming in to slot in at right-back.
And Kamara is taken off, with Dendoncker on in his place.
GOOD SAVE! McGinn goes long and Gabriel chooses to try and get across to cover the inside, allowing Diaby to get on the end of it.
He squares it to Watkins in the middle, but his first-time shot is straight at Raya.
Arsenal are making their first change now.
Martinelli hasn't shown as much of a threat in the second half, and he's going off for Trossard.
Arsenal win a free-kick to the left, and Odegaard shapes as if he's going to whip it in, but he leaves it to Rice.
He drills it low, but a deflection off Luiz's heels takes the power off it for Martinez.
McGinn's frustration at a Villa attack fizzling out gets the better of him, and he flies into a challenge on Odegaard.
He can have no complaints about that booking.
Trossard's loose pass gifts possession to Ramsey, but Arsenal quickly flood back in numbers.
The Villa substitute plays a one-two with Dendoncker as they work it down the left, but he can only win a corner.
Luiz keeps the ball in play with a lovely bit of skill but nearly sets Odegaard on the counter.
Cash rushes in to intercept the pass before that can happen and fizzes his low, long-range shot wide of the far post.
Rice just overruns the ball and then swings out a leg to stop Cash from getting to it.
He's the second Arsenal player to get a yellow card.
Villa's final roll of the dice is a straight swap at left-back.
Digne, who is on a booking, is replaced by Moreno.
Luiz's switch out to Cash is cut out, and Arsenal break quickly once more.
Havertz slides it through to Jesus, but as he tries to make a decision on which option to use, Moreno steps in to dispossess him.
Arsenal's second change is a swap up front as Nketiah comes on to add something different to their attack.
He replaces Jesus.
Arsenal have a knack for winning games late on, and they're still pushing for something from this one.
Cash plays out of their high press well, unlike Dendoncker, who slices it needlessly out of play for a Gunners throw-in.
Arsenal are still dominating possession, but Villa are standing firm at the back.
Their compact shape is doing more than enough to frustrate the visitors at the moment.
There's an off-the-ball incident between Carlos and Nketiah as the defender puts his arm across to stop the run.
He catches the substitute with his elbow, and though there's a VAR check for a possible red card, it's just a yellow.
NO GOAL! It's a great cross by Odegaard, and Havertz just rises above Cash.
The ball ricochets off both players a couple of times before the German eventually pokes it in from very close range.
He's ready to run off in celebration, but the referee says no goal for a handball by Havertz before he scored.
It was a bit of a scramble by both Havertz and Cash at the far post, and it does look like it bounced against Havertz's hand at some point during the chaos.
The referee gave it in real-time, and after a very long look at the replays, the onfield decision stands! Still 1-0 Villa!
Martinez was flailing behind Cash during the disallowed goal, and the right-back caught him in the eye with his boot as they both went down.
He's up celebrating the decision with the crowd, but he needs patching up before the game can carry on.
The final roll of the dice for Arsenal is an attacking one.
Zinchenko goes off, with Nelson adding another body up front.
BLOCK! McGinn makes a driving run upfield, but instead of using the options to his left, he goes it alone, running into Gabriel.
The rebound falls to Dendoncker, who curls a long-range shot on goal, but Saliba gets in the way of that one.
The board originally showed five additional minutes, but due to the VAR check at the start of stoppage time, we're still playing here.
Villa are trying their best to run the clock down and seal what would be a historic 15th consecutive home win.
MISS! Arsenal are throwing everything they have at Villa to get another last-gasp goal here.
Rice curls a good cross in, but Nketiah gets caught under it with his header looping over the bar.
The flag was up against him anyway.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 1-0 ARSENAL.
Aston Villa set a new club record of 15 consecutive home wins in the league as McGinn's early goal sees them beat Arsenal 1-0.
The Villa captain scored just seven minutes in, rifling his shot into the top corner.
They struggled to create too many more chances, but their defensive work caused Arsenal all sorts of problems.
Carlos made two goal-line clearances, one on either side of half-time, as he denied Martinelli and an own goal from a corner.

Saka did find the back of the net, but it was ruled out for offside, while Havertz thought he'd equalised in the 90th minute, but the referee spotted a handball in the build-up, and it was disallowed.
Villa stay in third, but that win means they're just one point behind the Gunners, and they're just two points off Liverpool at the top.
They play Zrinjski in the Europa Conference League on Thursday next time out.
Arsenal suffer just their second league defeat of the season as they miss the chance to go back into first.
They travel to PSV on Tuesday in the Champions League.
That's all for today, goodbye!
